content:
If you're a heavy user testing Apple Watch with this summer's beta, you may have noticed that some existing apps can't launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The related updates are being pushed via the App Store, with the "What's New" section reading: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27 and includes no new features."

Apple notified developers this week that this update process will be completed before August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is likely to be officially released to the public around mid-September, so the necessary related updates have been pushed ahead of schedule.

Apple stated that because some arm64 sections of watchOS apps have issues, they need to carry out this work first. It appears they are automatically reprocessing and repackaging the apps to fix binary compatibility issues, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers needing to take any action.
